@@ -427,10 +429,17 @@ class Context:
         #: Show option default values when formatting help text.
         self.show_default: bool | None = show_default
 
+        #: Enforce that all child contexts are closed before this
+        #: context is closed.
+        self.validate_nesting: bool = validate_nesting
+        self._child_contexts: set[Context] = set()
+
         self._close_callbacks: list[t.Callable[[], t.Any]] = []
         self._depth = 0
         self._parameter_source: dict[str, ParameterSource] = {}
         self._exit_stack = ExitStack()
+        #: Optional callback invoked with this context when it is closed.
+        self._on_exit: t.Callable[[Context], t.Any] | None = on_exit
 
     @property
     def protected_args(self) -> list[str]:
@@ -477,9 +486,11 @@ class Context:
         tb: TracebackType | None,
     ) -> None:
         self._depth -= 1
-        if self._depth == 0:
-            self.close()
-        pop_context()
+        try:
+            if self._depth == 0:
+                self.close()
+        finally:
+            pop_context()
 
     @contextmanager
     def scope(self, cleanup: bool = True) -> cabc.Iterator[Context]:
@@ -606,11 +617,36 @@ class Context:
         """Invoke all close callbacks registered with
         :meth:`call_on_close`, and exit all context managers entered
         with :meth:`with_resource`.
+
+        If :attr:`validate_nesting` is enabled and any child contexts
+        are still open, a :exc:`RuntimeError` is raised.
+
+        If an ``on_exit`` callback was given, it is invoked with this
+        context first. Exceptions raised by it are ignored so cleanup
+        always runs.
         """
+        if self.validate_nesting and self._child_contexts:
+            open_children = ", ".join(
+                sorted(repr(c.info_name) for c in self._child_contexts)
+            )
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"Cannot close context {self.info_name!r} while child contexts"
+                f" are still open: {open_children}."
+            )
+
+        if self._on_exit is not None:
+            try:
+                self._on_exit(self)
+            except Exception:
+                pass
+
         self._exit_stack.close()
         # In case the context is reused, create a new exit stack.
         self._exit_stack = ExitStack()
 
+        if self.parent is not None:
+            self.parent._child_contexts.discard(self)
+
     @property
     def command_path(self) -> str:
         """The computed command path.  This is used for the ``usage``
@@ -728,7 +764,17 @@ class Context:
 
         :meta private:
         """
-        return type(self)(command, info_name=command.name, parent=self)
+        sub_ctx = type(self)(
+            command,
+            info_name=command.name,
+            parent=self,
+            validate_nesting=self.validate_nesting,
+        )
+
+        if self.validate_nesting:
+            self._child_contexts.add(sub_ctx)
+
+        return sub_ctx
 
     @t.overload
     def invoke(
@@ -1123,6 +1169,7 @@ class Command:
         info_name: str | None,
         args: list[str],
         parent: Context | None = None,

         **extra: t.Any,
     ) -> Context:
         """This function when given an info name and arguments will kick

+        :param on_exit: optional callback invoked with the context when
+                        it is closed.
         :param extra: extra keyword arguments forwarded to the context
                       constructor.
 
@@ -1149,6 +1198,9 @@ class Command:
             if key not in extra:
                 extra[key] = value
 
+        if on_exit is not None:
+            extra["on_exit"] = on_exit
+
         ctx = self.context_class(self, info_name=info_name, parent=parent, **extra)
 
         with ctx.scope(cleanup=False):
